title: Heavy, Light and Where Sounds Come From
tagline: Tafkhim and tarqiq: full and thin letters, plus the map of the mouth.
intro: Some letters are said with a full, deep sound (heavy, tafkhim) and some with a thin, light sound (tarqiq). A few letters can be either, depending on their surroundings: ra and the lam of Allah. We finish with the map of where every letter is born in the mouth.

lessons.title: Heavy Letters
lessons.summary: Seven letters are always heavy: the back of the tongue rises toward the roof of the mouth and the sound is full and deep.
explain: The seven heavy letters (huroof al-isti'la) are خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ. A phrase to remember them: خُصَّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ.
To say them heavy, raise the back of the tongue toward the soft palate, round the lips a little, and keep the sound deep. Compare ص (heavy) with س (light), or ط with ت.
They stay heavy whatever vowel they carry, and they can make a neighboring alif sound fuller as well.
lessons.letters: خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ
how: Raise the back of the tongue.
Keep the sound deep and full, with no thinning, even with a kasrah.
lessons.spot: Any of خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ. There is no color for this rule.
tips: Say سَ then صَ to hear and feel the difference.
mistakes: Thinning a heavy letter when it has a kasrah, such as صِ or قِ.

examples.note: ٱلْمَغْضُوبِ: غ and ض are heavy.
ٱقْرَأْ and خَلَقَ: ق and خ are heavy.
قُلْ and ٱلْفَلَقِ: ق is heavy twice.

cards.a: خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ (خُصَّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ).

cards.q: Is a heavy letter still heavy when it has a kasrah?
cards.a: Yes. Heavy letters stay heavy whatever vowel they carry (for example the ص in صِرَٲطَ).

lessons.title: The Letter Ra
lessons.summary: Ra is heavy (full) or light (thin) depending on its vowel and on the letter before it.
explain: Heavy ra (tafkhim): a ra with a fathah or dammah (رَ رُ), and a ra sakinah after a fathah or dammah, as in أَرْسَلَ and يُرْزَقُونَ.
Light ra (tarqiq): a ra with a kasrah (رِ), and a ra sakinah after a kasrah, as in فِرْعَوْنَ.
Exception: a ra sakinah after a kasrah is heavy if a heavy letter (خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ) follows it in the same word, as in قِرْطَاسٍ.
Rules for stopping on a ra have a few more details. Ask your teacher once you are comfortable with these basics.
how: Look at the vowel on the ra, and if it has a sukun, at the vowel before it.
Fathah or dammah means heavy. Kasrah means light.
lessons.spot: Look at the vowel on or before the ra. There is no color for this rule.
tips: Heavy sounds like 'raw', light sounds like 'ree' (with the tongue tip lightly tapping).
mistakes: Thinning a heavy ra, or making a light ra too full.

examples.note: وَأَرْسَلَ: ra sakinah after fathah, heavy.
فِرْعَوْنَ: ra sakinah after kasrah, light.

cards.a: When it has a fathah or dammah, or is sakin after a fathah or dammah.
When it has a kasrah, or is sakin after a kasrah (unless a heavy letter follows in the same word).

lessons.title: The Lam of Allah
lessons.meaning: Heavy or light lam in the name Allah
lessons.summary: The lam in the name Allah is heavy after a fathah or dammah, and light after a kasrah.
explain: Heavy after a fathah or dammah: قَالَ ٱللَّهُ, هُوَ ٱللَّهُ. Also when you begin on the name.
Light after a kasrah: بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ, ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ.
Every other lam in the Quran is light.
how: Look at the vowel before the name.
Fathah or dammah: full lam. Kasrah: thin lam.
lessons.spot: The vowel on the letter just before the name Allah. There is no color for this rule.
tips: Bismillah is light; qul huwallahu is heavy.
mistakes: Making the lam heavy in Bismillah, or light in Qul huwallahu.

examples.note: Starting on the name: heavy lam.
نَصْرُ ٱللَّهِ: after a dammah, heavy lam.

cards.q: When is the lam of Allah heavy?
cards.a: After a fathah or dammah (and when starting on the name).

cards.q: When is the lam of Allah light?
cards.a: After a kasrah, as in بِسْمِ ٱللَّهِ.

lessons.title: Where Letters Come From
lessons.summary: Every Arabic letter has a home in the mouth. There are 17 homes grouped into 5 areas.
explain: 1. Al-Jawf (the open space of the mouth and throat): the three long-vowel letters ا و ي.
2. Al-Halq (the throat) in 3 zones: deepest ء ه, middle ع ح, nearest غ خ.
3. Al-Lisan (the tongue) holds 18 letters in 10 spots: ق ك | ج ش ي | ض | ل | ن | ر | ط د ت | ص س ز | ظ ذ ث.
4. Ash-Shafatan (the lips): ف from the lower lip and upper teeth, ب م و from the lips.
how: Practice each letter on its own, slowly, in front of a mirror.
Add a fathah and a sukun: أَبْ أَتْ أَثْ ...
tips: Say each letter with a sukun after a short hamza (like أَبْ) to feel exactly where it lands.

showcase.note: ع from the middle of the throat.
ق from the back of the tongue, ه from deep in the throat.
ب from the lips, ت from the tongue tip.

cards.q: How many articulation points (makharij) are there, in how many areas?
cards.a: 17 points in 5 areas: the open space (jawf), throat (halq), tongue (lisan), lips (shafatan) and nasal passage (khayshum).

cards.q: Which letters come from the throat?
cards.a: ء ه (deepest), ع ح (middle), غ خ (nearest).

cards.q: Which letters come from the lips?
cards.a: ف (lower lip + upper teeth), ب م و (the lips).

cards.q: Which letters come from the open space (al-jawf)?
cards.a: The three long-vowel letters: ا و ي.
